title: Microsoft 365 admin center: control publishing of agents with actions built in Teams Toolkit
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned publishing control from the documented upload and approval controls. The roadmap facts, licensing qualifications and rejection API are supported; the two UI paths could be extended to show the final configuration and publishing steps.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a new Microsoft 365 admin center control over whether makers can publish advanced agents with actions for their tenants.
claims.quote: To give admins control over whether agent makers can publish advanced agents (agents with actions) for their tenants, we are introducing a new control in the M365 admin center.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The planned control specifically applies to advanced agents created from Teams Toolkit.
claims.quote: This control specifically applies to advanced agents created from Teams Toolkit.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn calls the tool Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit and says it was previously known as Teams Toolkit.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit (previously known as Teams Toolkit) for Visual Studio Code built on top of the Teams App Submission API

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page explicitly describing this roadmap item as the planned Teams Toolkit publishing control.
claims.quote: Searched: 487847 Teams Toolkit publishing control default license rollout; Teams Toolkit advanced agents default control. Opened toolkit/publish, configure-copilot-advanced-package-uploads and agent-requests; no explicit identification of the roadmap control.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The planned control's default and what happens on arrival are not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit advanced agents default control; 487847 Teams Toolkit publishing control default license rollout. Read the roadmap, advanced package uploads, agent requests and agent settings; none states the planned control's arrival default.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the applicable product-level entitlement, with feature-specific requirements left unpublished.
claims.quote: The following licensing options include agents that can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agent management requires the applicable Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, or Microsoft Agent 365 subscription and licenses.
claims.quote: Your organization has the required subscription and licenses for either Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, or Microsoft Agent 365.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licensing requirement specific to the planned control, including an Agent 365 requirement for its UI, is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit publishing control licensing meter; Teams Toolkit control publish license. Opened agent-365-overview licensing and prerequisites, advanced package uploads and copilotpackage-reject; only general entitlements and the API license are stated.

claims.claim: No meter specific to the roadmap control is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit publishing control licensing meter; Teams Toolkit agents with actions publishing admin control default licensing meter. Read agent-365-overview, advanced package uploads and the roadmap; no meter for configuring this control is stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no license or meter.
claims.quote: To give admins control over whether agent makers can publish advanced agents (agents with actions) for their tenants, we are introducing a new control in the M365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Advanced package uploads prerequisites name AI Admin and admin center access, but no license.
claims.quote: To access and manage the Copilot advanced package uploads setting, you need access to the Microsoft 365 admin center and the following administrator role: - Edit sharing settings: AI Admin

claims.claim: Advanced package uploads is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Settings > All settings > Advanced package uploads.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings > All settings > Advanced package uploads. The Advanced package uploads pane is displayed.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Copilot > Settings > All settings > Advanced package uploads > All users / No users / Specific users or groups', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/configure-copilot-advanced-package-uploads; the current path correctly reaches the setting pane.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn Graph or PowerShell call is documented for the Advanced package uploads setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Advanced package uploads Graph PowerShell API settings; advanced package uploads API; Advanced package uploads PowerShell Graph. Read configure-copilot-advanced-package-uploads, copilotpolicysetting and utcm-copilot-resources; no operation sets this control.

claims.claim: Advanced package uploads is an organization-wide setting controlling who can upload advanced agent and plugin packages.
claims.quote: You can control who in your organization can upload advanced agent and plugin packages in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: A package using a Declarative Agent with actions is an advanced agent package.
claims.quote: An advanced agent is a package that uses either a Declarative Agent with actions or an MCP server.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A package using an MCP server is also an advanced agent package.
claims.quote: An advanced agent is a package that uses either a Declarative Agent with actions or an MCP server.

claims.claim: The Advanced package uploads setting does not affect basic package uploads, which remain allowed.
claims.quote: Basic package uploads remain allowed and aren't impacted.

claims.claim: Advanced package uploads applies only to user-uploaded packages from organization members.
claims.quote: This setting only applies to user-uploaded packages by members of your organization

claims.claim: Advanced package uploads does not relate to Microsoft or third-party built agents.
claims.quote: doesn't relate to Microsoft or third-party built agents.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify Advanced package uploads as the control in the roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: 487847 Teams Toolkit publishing control default license rollout; advanced package uploads API. Read advanced package uploads, toolkit/publish and agent requests; the upload page gives no roadmap ID or explicit equivalence with the planned publishing control.

claims.claim: The Agents Toolkit organization publish step submits the app to the Teams admin center rather than directly publishing it to the organization store.
claims.quote: The app doesn't publish to your organization's app store yet. The step submits the app to the Teams admin center where you can approve it for publishing to your organization's app store.

claims.claim: An administrator can approve that app for publication to the organization's app store in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Select the status dropdown and change from Submitted to Publish. After you publish the app, the publishing status changes to Published and the status automatically changes to Allowed.

claims.claim: Agents made with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit can be submitted for approval in Microsoft 365 admin center Requests.
claims.quote: agents that members of your organization create by using Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, or Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit can be submitted for admin approval.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Agents with actions can invoke custom actions against connected systems.
claims.quote: Confirm the capabilities, data sources, security and permissions, and custom actions that the agent can invoke.

claims.claim: Requested agent details show capabilities, data sources and custom actions before publication.
claims.quote: From the Requests list, you can select the agent to see the details about the agent to better understand the agent's capabilities, data sources, and custom actions before allowing the agent to be published to your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs reviewers to confirm requested agents' capabilities, data sources, permissions and custom actions.
claims.quote: Select the requested agent and view the agent's details. Confirm the capabilities, data sources, security and permissions, and custom actions that the agent can invoke.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].governs; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tenant publication requires an administrator's per-agent approval or rejection rather than a tenant-wide Requests switch.
claims.quote: When a member of your organization publishes an agent to your tenant, the agent requires administrator approval before becoming available tenant-wide. Administrators can review the agent's details, such as the description, owner, data, and tools, and then publish or reject it.

claims.claim: The Requests publishing wizard includes Review permissions, where the administrator grants consent to requested permissions if appropriate.
claims.quote: In the Review permissions step, view the permissions requested by the agent and grant admin consent if appropriate. Permissions allow the agent to access relevant data or perform actions on behalf of users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The new control's effect on data review and consent is not described; the documented consent step is in Requests.
claims.quote: Searched: 487847 Teams Toolkit publishing control default license rollout; Teams Toolkit agents with actions publishing admin control. Read roadmap, agent-requests and advanced package uploads; no consent or data-review mechanism is assigned to the planned control.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether the planned control also covers MCP servers is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit publishing control rollout MCP pending. Read roadmap, advanced package uploads and agent-settings; MCP is included in the existing upload setting, but no source identifies the planned publishing control's MCP scope.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit publishing control rollout MCP pending; Teams Toolkit agents with actions publishing admin control existing agents pending requests. Read advanced package uploads, agent-requests and roadmap; no retroactive effect of the planned control is described.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit publishing control rollout MCP pending; Teams Toolkit agents with actions publishing admin control existing agents pending requests. Read roadmap, advanced package uploads and agent-requests; no planned-control effect on existing pending submissions is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether a Message center post will announce this planned control.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced package uploads offers All users, allowing all users to upload advanced agent and plugin packages.
claims.quote: All users: All users can upload advanced agent and plugin packages.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Advanced package uploads offers No users, preventing users from uploading advanced agent and plugin packages.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Requests > agent exposes Publish to store and Reject submission.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents > Requests. ... select Publish to store within the agent details pane to view the agent publishing wizard. ... Reject submission - After reviewing a requested agent's details, select this action
claims.fix: Keep the documented rejection route. Extend the publishing route to 'Agents > All agents > Requests > agent > Publish to store > users or groups > policy template > existing template / default template / custom template > Review permissions > Publish' at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-requests; Publish to store starts, rather than completes, publishing.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject is the documented Graph operation for rejecting a pending package submission.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The API rejects a pending package submission only, not an individual user's request.
claims.quote: Reject a pending Copilot package title submission. This action reviews a package title and its submitted version; it doesn't reject an individual user's request.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The rejection API is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The rejection request body's version property is optional in the schema.
claims.quote: version | String | Version of the staged package title submission to reject. Optional in the schema; use the matching submitted version to target a specific review.

claims.claim: The rejection request body's reviewerComment property is optional.
claims.quote: reviewerComment | String | Optional explanation for the rejection.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs callers to supply the version of the staged submission being rejected.
claims.quote: Supply the version of the staged submission you're rejecting.

claims.claim: Omitting version does not select the latest or pending submission version.
claims.quote: The schema defines both parameters as optional. This doesn't mean that omitting version selects the latest or pending version.

claims.claim: The Graph copilotPolicySetting reference lists five supported Copilot settings other than package uploads.
claims.quote: Pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat; Block Copilot Access to Open Content; Control access to Designer Image Generation; Allow web search in Copilot; Control Admin Copilot availability in Microsoft 365 Admin Center

claims.claim: The Tenant Configuration Management Copilot resources page lists no package upload setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Advanced package uploads Graph PowerShell API settings. Opened and read the complete utcm-copilot-resources page and its 20 resource descriptions; none configures advanced agent or plugin package uploads.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access controls which types of agents and plugins users can view and install from the catalog.
claims.quote: The Agent and plugin access setting controls which types of agents and plugins users can view and install from the agent catalog.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access includes organization-built agents and governs installation rather than maker publishing permission.
claims.quote: Allow agents and plugins built by your organization - Enables users to install custom agents and plugins developed within your tenant.

claims.claim: No source states that the planned control changes existing behavior on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Toolkit advanced agents default control; Teams Toolkit publishing control rollout MCP pending. Read roadmap, advanced package uploads and agent-requests; no automatic change to existing behavior is specified for the planned control.
